title: Reservoir-to-Realtime Capacity Roadmap and Ops Bakeoff
creator: Ava Chen
description: Quarterly initiative to convert our static reservoir capacity model into a hybrid reservoir-to-realtime autoscale pipeline. Goal is to reduce cold-start latency for dedicated customers while maintaining cost SLAs. Deliverables include: canary experiment framework, new autoscale policy primitives, prewarm/eviction heuristics, dashboards, and ops playbooks. Emphasis on operational readiness, rollback criteria, and cost delta monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: Canary reduces median cold-start P95 by >=20% for targeted workloads
New autoscale policy supports fast-path scale-up within 90s for priority slices
No more than 5% increase in steady-state committed spend vs baseline in test zones
Runbook for oncall with clear rollback and mitigation steps documented
Console dashboards show token-level cost delta and warm-pool utilization
milestones: Design spike and API contract freeze - 2026-02-20
comments: 2026-02-12 - Ava Chen: Kickoff with Eng/Infra/Observability. Agreed scope: focus on priority slices (finance + chat) for initial canary.
2026-02-18 - Marcus Li (Eng): Spike showed kernel-queue contention under concurrent prewarm. Proposed moving warm allocation earlier in request path — ENG spike created ENG-1987.
2026-02-22 - Sofia Patel: Trade-off discussion — tolerate up to 5% cost uplift for 20% latency gains. PM/Finance approved provisional budget for canary.
2026-02-26 - Design review (Monica Reed): Dashboard mockups approved with minor copy changes (see drive link). UX asked for clearer failure state CTA.
2026-03-01 - Rafael Gomez (SRE): Added runbook draft, included fallback to smaller model family and regional failover; marked security_review_required = false for now.
decision_log: Prefer hybrid reservoir+realtime model vs full realtime to limit cost exposure
Canary limited to two regions and two customer tenants to reduce blast radius
Autoscale policy will expose 'priority slice' flag to route warm-pool reservations
implementation_notes: Autoscale primitives implemented as declarative policy objects in orchestration service.
KV-cache warm hints propagated from routing layer; requires minor contract change (see PR 4621).
Batching heuristics adjusted: prewarm allocation triggers when short-tail queue length > 8.
risks: Risk of overprovisioning causing commit spend spike if warm heuristics misfire
Operational complexity increases for oncall; mitigated by runbook and training
Edge cases for multi-tenant noisy neighbors; dependency on fairshare throttling
qa_plan: Synthetic load tests with mixed prompt lengths and cold sequences
Customer-seeded trials with two beta tenants, run under observability gates
Chaos tests: region failover and rapid scale-down scenarios
notes: This doc replaces earlier 'adaptive-reservation' experiments with a narrower ops bakeoff focus.
We will coordinate launches with sales/AE for beta customer selection and communications.
